Description: The construction and refinement of mathematical, statistical, or computational models used to simulate, predict, or analyze biological or clinical phenomena.
Software tools, algorithms, databases, or computing infrastructure developed or used to support computational research and data analysis.

Efforts and practices that promote fair representation, equal opportunity, and inclusion of individuals from diverse backgrounds, identities, and abilities within research and educational communities.
The diminished or absent response of cancer cells or tumors to a therapeutic agent (resistance), or their degree of susceptibility to being affected or killed by that agent (sensitivity).
The study of heritable changes in gene expression or cellular phenotype caused by mechanisms other than alterations in the underlying DNA sequence, such as DNA methylation and histone modification.
The process by which populations of organisms change over successive generations through mechanisms such as mutation, genetic drift, and natural selection.
The design, generation, and validation of laboratory-based systems, such as cell lines, organoids, or animal models, used to study disease biology or evaluate therapeutic interventions.
The quality or state of consisting of elements that are not of the same kind or nature, such as variability among cells, tissues, or tumors within a biological system.
Therapy designed to induce, enhance, or suppress changes in a patient's immune status in order to treat disease, such as cancer.
The study of how mechanical forces and the physical properties of cells and tissues influence gene expression and genetic regulation.
The study of how mechanical properties of, or forces acting on, cells and tissues contribute to resistance against therapeutic agents or other stressors.
The organic biochemical processes within a cell or organism that are necessary to sustain life, encompassing both anabolic (biosynthetic) and catabolic (degradative) reactions.
The spread of cancer cells from the primary tumor site to other parts of the body, forming secondary tumors that share characteristics of the original neoplasm.
The design, optimization, and validation of new experimental techniques, protocols, or assays for measuring biological or clinical phenomena.

The cellular and molecular environment surrounding a tumor or biological system, including neighboring cells, blood vessels, immune cells, signaling molecules, and the extracellular matrix, that influences its growth and behavior.
Cellular stress arising from the activation of oncogenes or dysregulated growth signaling, which can trigger protective responses such as senescence or apoptosis.
A resource topic that does not fit within any of the other defined categories.
Activities and programs designed to engage, inform, or provide resources to communities, patients, or the public outside of a research institution's core scientific work.
The creation and refinement of technological, computational, or experimental platforms and infrastructure that support research workflows or data generation.
A document or other resource, such as a tutorial, course, or teaching module, designed for learning, educational, or training purposes.
A pathologic process in which molecular alterations result in a more aggressive cytologic and phenotypic profile and clinical course of a neoplasm over time.
The study of the interactions between the immune system and tumor cells, including immune surveillance, immune evasion, and immune-based responses to cancer.
The study of the structure, theory, and application of computational systems, algorithms, and information processing using mathematical, logical, and empirical methods.
The interdisciplinary scientific study of external biotic and abiotic factors to which an organism is exposed, and their effects on health and ecosystems.

The field of knowledge, theory, and technology concerned with the collection, organization, storage, retrieval, and dissemination of facts and data, including aspects of communication, publishing, and informatics.
The systematic identification, development, organization, and use of educational resources, tools, and equipment, including audiovisual and digital aids, to support teaching and learning.
The study of the structure of living organisms and their parts (anatomy) together with the functions and mechanisms of those structures (physiology).
The scientific study of living organisms, including their structure, function, growth, evolution, and interactions with their environment.
The branch of biology concerned with the relationships between organisms and their environment.
The branch of biology that deals with heredity, especially the mechanisms of hereditary transmission and the variation of inherited characteristics among similar or related organisms.
The processes by which an organism consumes and utilizes food, water, and other nourishment necessary to sustain its life processes.
An educational topic area covering skills and concepts related to measuring quantities and to collecting, representing, and interpreting data.
The application of statistical methods and probability theory to describe, summarize, and draw inferences from data.
The scientific study of the composition, structure, properties, and reactions of matter, especially atomic and molecular systems.
The scientific study of matter, energy, and the fundamental forces and laws governing their interactions and behavior in nature.

An interdisciplinary field that studies complex interactions within biological systems using a holistic approach, integrating computational and mathematical modeling with experimental data to understand emergent properties of the system as a whole.
Efforts to promote, protect, and represent the rights, needs, and interests of patients, often through education, support services, or engagement in research and health policy processes.
